newsitem.title: UK: Russian seaborne crude exports fall in Feb - Petrak.
newsitem.headline: Russian seaborne crude exports fall in Feb - Petrak.

text.p: Russian seaborne crude exports fell almost five percent, or 60,000 barrels per day (bpd), in February as a slide in Novorossiisk shipments masked higher volumes from other Black Sea ports, shipping inspectors Petrak said on Tuesday.
Crude exports from the four ports, including Tuapse, Odessa and the Baltic port of Ventspils, totalled 1.154 million bpd, 57,000 bpd fewer than in January, Petrak said.
Russia's leading port of Novorossiisk shipped 538,583 bpd in February, against 633,959 bpd in January, a 15 percent fall caused mainly by weather-related disruption to loadings.
Odessa shipped 233,997 bpd, up 19,532 bpd on January, while Tuapse saw exports rise to 95,300 bpd from 73,460 bpd.
February exports from the Latvian port of Ventspils totalled 285,752 bpd, little changed from January's 289,656 bpd, Petrak said.
